text: dsh-acp-server 是面向 Zed、其他 ACP v1 客户端和脚本的 DeepSeek Harness 插件，将 DSH agent 接入 ACP。它可通过 stdio 提供编辑器连接，也可独立运行 HTTP+SSE 服务，或挂载到 DSH Web 共用端口。用户能创建、提示、列出、恢复和删除会话，切换模型与推理强度，并由客户端处理权限询问；脚本还可异步派发任务、等待和取消。可选主机控制桥接让 ACP 客户端调用 DSH 的远程方法。需要 Node.js 22 及 DSH CLI；远程连接可配置 bearer token。

dsh-acp-server connects DSH agents to ACP clients over stdio or HTTP+SSE, including on the shared DSH Web port. It supports persistent sessions, model selection, permission prompts, task orchestration, and optional host control. Requires Node.js 22 and DSH.

dsh-acp-server 的功能「ACP 多传输接入」：将 DSH agent 暴露给 ACP 客户端。启动时可选 stdio、独立 HTTP+SSE，或注册到现有 Web 服务的 /acp 路由。
dsh-acp-server 的功能「持久会话」：客户端可创建新会话、提示 agent、列出已有会话、恢复会话并回放转录，也能关闭或删除持久化会话。
dsh-acp-server 的功能「脚本任务编排」：通过 dsh/sessions/prompt 排队或转向发送提示并立即返回，再用 wait 查询任务状态，或 cancel 取消运行中的会话。
dsh-acp-server 的功能「会话模型选择」：客户端可读取模型目录并为当前会话选择 provider/model；支持的模型路由还会提供 reasoning_effort 选项。
dsh-acp-server 的功能「DSH 主机控制」：启用 hostControl 后，ACP 客户端可查询实时远程方法目录、调用单次方法、订阅流式方法并取消流。
dsh-acp-server 的功能「远程方法命令行」：随附 CLI 的 catalog、call、stream 和 rpc 子命令，可输出方法目录、调用或流式读取结果，也能发送 ACP 请求。
dsh-acp-server 使用前须知：远程 HTTP serve 建议设置 bearer token；hostControl 默认开启，客户端能以操作者身份调用 DSH 方法。可关闭 hostControl。

**Agent Client Protocol (ACP) server for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`).**

Drive a full dsh coding agent - streaming output, tool calls, permission prompts, durable sessions - from [Zed](https://zed.dev) or any ACP v1 client, exactly like opencode or Gemini CLI.

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

dsh-acp-server README · What it does：A [`dsh` profile bundle](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) that boots the entire DeepSeek Harness (agent loop, tools, sandbox, session persistence) with an ACP v1 JSON-RPC server instead of - or alongside - the web UI.

dsh-acp-server README · What it does：| ACP method | Status |
|---|---|
| `initialize` | ✅ full capability advertisement (`loadSession`, `promptCapabilities.image`, `sessionCapabilities.list/resume/close/delete`) |
| `authenticate` | ✅ no-op success (dsh credentials live outside ACP; empty `authMethods`) |
| `session/new` | ✅ durable dsh agent + modes + slash-command advertisement + initial `configOptions` |
| `session/prompt` | ✅ streaming `agent_message_chunk` / `agent_thought_chunk` (reasoning), `plan` updates, full tool-call lifecycle, `{stopReason, usage}`; failed turns reject with a JSON-RPC error carrying the cause; **image blocks** persist through the dsh attachments service; a single `/command` text block routes to the dsh command registry |
| `session/set_config_option` | ✅ per-session `model` (`<provider>/<model>`) and `reasoning_effort` overrides; live effect on the next step; unsupported knobs/values refuse with precise `-32602`; `config_option_update` pushed on change |
| `usage_update` / `usage` | ✅ context usage (`used`/`size`) pushed from token accounting; the prompt response sums the turn's tokens (experimental ACP field) |
| `session/list` | ✅ every persisted + li

dsh-acp-server README · What it does：Roadmap: `session/fork` (still UNSTABLE in the ACP SDK), URL-mode elicitation, audio, document sync (`document/didOpen` et al. — this server is deliberately single-conversation); the dsh↔dsh client half, discovery, and identity are planned as a **separate package** - see [the design doc](research/acp-dsh-design.md).

dsh-acp-server README · The two final forms：```bash
dsh-acp-server       # 1) standalone: ACP on stdio (editors), or `serve` for remote HTTP
dsh web              # 2) together: the GUI and ACP in one process on one port
```

dsh-acp-server README · Form 1 — standalone (`dsh-acp-server`)：After `npm i -g dsh-acp-server` (or via `npx`). The bin boots `dsh --profile acp` with the current stdio and passes every launcher flag through (`serve --port 7800`, `--patch extra.yml`). First use in a DSH home auto-bootstraps the `acp` profile with the official `dsh plugin` command - bootstrap output goes to stderr, so an editor's stdout only ever sees ACP frames.

Zed → Settings → `agent_servers` (full sample in [examples/zed-settings.json](examples/zed-settings.json)):

dsh-acp-server README · Form 2 — together (`dsh web`)：Install into the `web` profile once; every plain `dsh web` boot then serves the GUI and ACP on one port:

```bash
node bin/setup-webacp.mjs        # official `dsh plugin --profile web add` + the web-mounted row
dsh web                          # http://127.0.0.1:3080 = GUI, /acp = ACP
node bin/acp-chat.mjs --url http://127.0.0.1:3080
```

Prefer to keep `web` untouched? `node bin/setup-webacp.mjs --clone webacp` gives the same on `dsh --profile webacp`.

dsh-acp-server README · Form 2 — together (`dsh web`)：The script writes a row-level `inject: [agents, agentDefaultModel, webServer]` so Cordis starts the acp-server fiber only after the shared `webServer` service exists - the stdio transport can never race a web boot. A hand install without that row is safe too: the plugin web-mounts late via service provisioning (terminal boots skip stdio entirely; daemon boots get an EOF grace window). The full row is documented in [examples/patches/web-mounted.yml](examples/patches/web-mounted.yml).

dsh-acp-server README · Form 2 — together (`dsh web`)：Why a bin instead of the literal `dsh acp-server`: the dsh launcher hardcodes its app subcommands (`web`, `plugin`) and parses argv before any plugin loads, so a bundle cannot register one; the wrapper is the same single-command shape.

dsh-acp-server README · Drive dsh from a script (`run`)：`dsh-acp-server run` is a one-shot CLI for **external agents and orchestrators**: it spawns the real `dsh --profile acp`, speaks ACP to it through the same SDK every other client uses, prints the answer, and exits. No ACP client implementation required:

dsh-acp-server README · Drive dsh from a script (`run`)：```bash
dsh-acp-server run "fix the failing tests and summarize the cause" \
  --cwd /path/to/workspace \
  --json                                  # one JSON object on stdout
  --session acp-69041a38-...              # resume a persisted session (no cold plugin-tree start)

dsh-acp-server README · Drive dsh from a script (`run`)：- **Default output** is the final assistant answer as plain text on stdout; progress (tool calls, permission notes) goes to stderr. `--json` prints exactly one object: `{sessionId, stopReason, text, toolCalls: [{title, status}], usage?, error?}`.
- **Exit codes**: `0` done · `1` error · `2` timeout (the turn was cancelled) · `3` cancelled · `4` a permission request was denied. A script branches on the code, never on parsing prose.
- `--session <id>` resumes a persisted session (`dsh-acp-server run ... --session "$(cat last-session)"` keeps one conversation across invocations); without it each run creates a fresh session.
- `--model <provider>/<model>` maps to `session/set_config_option` and overrides the profile default for that session only; your profile's `agent-default-model` is untouched.
- `--permission-policy auto` approves every permission request (allow once), `deny` rejects them (exit `4` if any was rejected), `ask` (default) prompts on the terminal — and fails closed (deny) when stdin is not a TTY.

dsh-acp-server README · Install：Requires Node.js ≥ 22 and the `dsh` CLI (`npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh`). The `dsh-acp-server` bin handles the profile itself; to manage it explicitly:

```bash
dsh-acp-server README · prebuilt from npm (recommended - no build authorization needed)：dsh plugin --profile acp add dsh-acp-server

dsh-acp-server README · Remote access (`serve`)：Editors get ACP over stdio; `serve` runs a long-lived HTTP+SSE endpoint for remote machines, shared agents, or curl - following the shape of the ACP [streamable-HTTP RFD](https://agentclientprotocol.com/rfds/streamable-http-websocket-transport.md):

```bash
dsh --profile acp serve --port 7800            # bind 127.0.0.1 by default
dsh --profile acp serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 7800 --token s3cret
```

dsh-acp-server README · Remote access (`serve`)：The serve port also ships a built-in single-file web client at `GET /` - open
http://127.0.0.1:7800 in any browser for a complete chat UI (streaming,
thoughts, tool cards, plans, permission dialogs) driven purely by the ACP
routes above. It is the reference proof that this surface can carry a web
interface. The same routes are served in web-mounted mode (Form 2) on the
GUI's port.

dsh-acp-server README · HTTP transport reference：| Method + path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `POST /acp` | one JSON-RPC message per body (single JSON object or NDJSON lines); `initialize` → `200` + JSON body + `Acp-Connection-Id` header; everything else → `202`, the response arrives on the SSE stream |
| `GET /acp/stream` | long-lived SSE stream for the connection (header `Acp-Connection-Id`, or `?connection=`); `: ping` comment every 15 s |
| `DELETE /acp` | close the connection → `204` |
| `GET /acp/healthz` | liveness probe (no auth; serve mode also answers `/healthz`) |

dsh-acp-server README · HTTP transport reference：Errors: `401` bad/missing credentials · `404` unknown connection id or route · `400` unparseable body. Several clients can attach to one process (one ACP connection each).

dsh-acp-server README · dsh/* vendor extensions (host plane)：ACP v1 standardizes one conversation, not the host around it. Sessions history,
jobs, goals, skills, and the live agent tree are exposed as vendor methods
under the `dsh/` namespace. Host writes and orchestration are described below:

dsh-acp-server README · dsh/* vendor extensions (host plane)：| Method | Returns |
|---|---|
| `dsh/sessions/list` | every persisted + live session (id, title, createdAt, cwd, parentSession, `acp` flag) |
| `dsh/sessions/read` | one session's transcript as `{seq, type, text}` entries |
| `dsh/sessions/search` | find sessions by ID, title, or cwd (`{query, limit?}`) |
| `dsh/sessions/resume` | reopen a persisted session as a live ACP session (full context) |
| `dsh/jobs/list` | background jobs (id, kind, label, status, owner) |
| `dsh/goals/list` | active goal per live agent (objective, phase, rounds) |
| `dsh/skills/list` | installed skills (name, description, provider) |
| `dsh/agents/tree` | live agents with parent/model/cwd (the subagent tree) |
| `dsh/sessions/watch` / `unwatch` | subscribe to any session's translated live stream - `dsh/session/update` frames in the same SessionUpdate shapes the owner gets (orchestrators, dashboards, audit) |

dsh-acp-server README · Orchestration and host control：Use `session/list` and `dsh/sessions/search` to locate work, then `session/resume` or `session/load` to switch to it. `dsh/sessions/prompt` queues or steers a turn and returns immediately; `dsh/sessions/wait`, `read`, and `watch` follow its outcome. `dsh/sessions/cancel` cancels a running turn, and `configure` sets its permission policy. `session/new` accepts `_meta['dsh/agentPreset']` and `_meta['dsh/permissionPolicy']` before the first turn.

dsh-acp-server README · Orchestration and host control：`dsh/remote/catalog` exposes the live Typert method catalog, parameter schemas, and an `available` flag. `dsh/remote/invoke` calls a unary method with `{endpoint, args}`. `dsh/remote/stream` opens a stream that sends `dsh/remote/item` and `dsh/remote/end`; `dsh/remote/cancel` stops it. The standalone ACP profile mounts workspace, directory browser, workspace files, and settings controllers. When mounted into `dsh web`, the bridge also sees that composition's other host methods. For example, `workspace/create` takes `{"endpoint":"workspace/create","args":{"request":{"path":"/absolute/project"}}}`. Inspect `settings/describe` and the catalog schema before calling `settings/update`. These calls run as the local DSH operator. Web-mounted ACP accepts a DSH Web login cookie or a configured ACP bearer token for scripts; standalone `serve` takes `--token`.

dsh-acp-server README · Orchestration and host control：The shell client uses the same ACP methods:

```bash
dsh-acp-server catalog workspace --url http://127.0.0.1:3080 --token "$DSH_ACP_TOKEN"
dsh-acp-server call workspace/create '{"request":{"path":"/absolute/project"}}' --url http://127.0.0.1:3080 --token "$DSH_ACP_TOKEN"
dsh-acp-server rpc dsh/sessions/search '{"query":"project"}' --url http://127.0.0.1:3080 --token "$DSH_ACP_TOKEN"
dsh-acp-server stream workspace/follow --limit 1 --url http://127.0.0.1:3080 --token "$DSH_ACP_TOKEN"

dsh-acp-server README · Orchestration and host control：`--url` and `--token` also read `DSH_ACP_URL` and `DSH_ACP_TOKEN`. Without a URL the CLI starts a private stdio server. `--detach` requires a running server and prints the session ID immediately; use `rpc dsh/sessions/wait '{"sessionId":"..."}'` and `rpc dsh/sessions/read` to follow the result. `--preset` selects the agent preset when creating a session. `call`, `stream`, and `rpc` accept inline JSON, `@file.json`, or `-` for stdin. Stream item limits must be positive integers; timeout values must be positive finite seconds. Stream timeout exits with code 2.

dsh-acp-server README · Orchestration and host control：The `run` client handles form questions: `auto` selects the first offered option, `deny` declines, and `ask` prompts in a terminal. With non-TTY stdin, `ask` answers questions with the first options; permission requests are denied. Detached tasks use the server's configured policy. The question tool must be present in the agent's composition.

dsh-acp-server README · Orchestration and host control：Push: `dsh/changed {topics}` notifications fire on turn ends, session
lifecycle, job changes, and agent-status transitions (throttled). **Interop-safe by construction** - they are sent
only to connections that opted in via the schema-sanctioned extension point
`clientCapabilities._meta['dsh/extensions']` (the `_meta` record is official
ACP schema); standard clients like Zed see a fully standard server and are
never contacted with vendor traffic. Each method degrades to a clean `-32601`
in compositions that lack the underlying service.

dsh-acp-server README · Orchestration and host control：A complete, runnable conversation with nothing but curl: [examples/curl-conversation.sh](examples/curl-conversation.sh).

```bash
./examples/curl-conversation.sh http://127.0.0.1:7800 [bearer-token]
```

dsh-acp-server README · Configuration：All knobs have schema defaults; override only the keys you want in your profile layer (`$DSH_HOME/profiles/<name>/cordis.patch.yml`). Full samples in [examples/patches/](examples/patches/).

dsh-acp-server README · Configuration：| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agentName` | string | `dsh` | `initialize.agentInfo.name` shown to clients |
| `provider` | string | - | pin the model for ACP sessions (must be set **with** `model`) |
| `model` | string | - | pin the model for ACP sessions (must be set **with** `provider`) |
| `token` | string | - | extra ACP bearer credential for web-mounted mode; otherwise DSH Web's login cookie is required. Standalone `serve` takes `--token` |
| `offerAlwaysPermissions` | boolean | `true` | include `allow_always` / `reject_always` options in permission requests |
| `flushOnTurnEnd` | boolean | `true` | flush session persistence after every completed turn |
| `hostControl` | boolean | `true` | expose `dsh/remote/*` host methods |
| `hostControlDeny` | string[] | `[]` | block endpoints such as `settings/*`, `workspace/delete`, or `*` |

dsh-acp-server README · Configuration：```yaml
- id: acp-server
  config:
    agentName: my-dsh
    provider: liepin        # pin (or omit both to follow the live default)

dsh-acp-server README · Configuration：Behavior follows the harness config conventions: the schema validates at plugin load (wrong types or a half-set provider/model pin fail loudly with the exact key), missing keys fall back to defaults (a patch layer replaces the whole config value, the schema refills the rest), and an unset provider/model follows the profile's `agent-default-model` - read **per session**, so in-GUI model switches apply to new ACP sessions too.
dsh-acp-server README · Configuration：Model credentials come from the usual dsh places (`$DSH_HOME` settings / provider API-key envs), shared with the web UI - no second setup.

dsh-acp-server README · Try it without an editor：`acp-chat` is a zero-install interactive terminal client bundled in this repo (REPL with streaming, tool-call display, plan rendering, and inline permission prompts). It speaks both transports:

```bash
node bin/acp-chat.mjs                                   # spawns `dsh --profile acp` (stdio)
node bin/acp-chat.mjs --url http://127.0.0.1:7800 --token s3cret   # remote HTTP+SSE
```

dsh-acp-server README · How it works：Transport choice is deterministic at mount: `serve` subcommand → standalone HTTP server; a `webServer` service present (or arriving late) → routes registered on the shared server; otherwise stdio.

```
ACP client (Zed / curl / acp-chat)
   │  stdio NDJSON JSON-RPC          │  HTTP POST + SSE (serve / web-mounted)
   ▼                                 ▼
  dsh-acp-server plugin ⇄ dsh services

dsh-acp-server README · How it works：Source layout: `src/connection.ts` (method handlers) · `translate.ts` / `config-options.ts` (pure wire mappings, unit-tested) · `event-bridge.ts` / `perm-bridge.ts` (dsh ⇄ ACP seams) · `session-delete.ts` (guarded persisted-session cleanup) · `cli/run.ts` (the one-shot CLI; `cli/run-core.ts` is its pure mapping layer) · `http-transport.ts` (shared HTTP router) · `serve-startup.ts` (the `serve` subcommand) · `config.ts` (schema) · `table.ts` (session registry).

dsh-acp-server README · How it works：Full research behind every mapping: [`research/`](research/) - [ACP protocol](research/acp-protocol.md), [DSH architecture](research/dsh-architecture.md), [prior art](research/acp-implementations.md), [design blueprint](research/acp-dsh-design.md).
